task.goal: Compile a governed Builder contract for the SuperVisuals single-frame portrait/quote/stat graphic format, without generating or editing any final image.
task.success_condition: The compiled contract preserves category binding, all activative semantic lineage refs, and the format's wrong-reading locks intact and unmutated.
task.atomic_boundary: One ratified SuperVisuals reference specimen set becomes one structural Builder contract; no image rendering or asset editing happens inside this harness.

source_expression_moment.description: The specific claim, quote, stat, or reaction being rendered into a single SuperVisuals frame.

voice_context.description: Who is pictured/speaking and in what register: attributed quote, opinion hot-take, stat callout, or reaction-meme pose.

activative_input.hidden_pressure: The scroll-speed audience needs to feel a claim is credible and worth stopping for before they check who actually said it or whether the wording is exact.
activative_input.stance: Attributive and declarative -- presents someone's stated claim, stat, or reaction as the whole frame.
stakes: implying an endorsement that was not actually given
activative_input.participation_design: One dominant claim per frame, resolved in under two seconds of attention, with a clear single source signal (portrait plus name or handle) instead of unattributed text.
activative_input.intended_reaction: The viewer accepts the claim as genuinely spoken or held by the pictured source and reads the full line before deciding whether to keep scrolling.
activative_input.smallest_useful_commitment: Read the full quoted or stated line before deciding whether to share or scroll past.
wrong_reading_locks: Do not let the bold pull-quote or stat text_block inside overlay_zone be read as a verbatim sourced quote or an already-verified statistic -- several specimens present paraphrased predictions or aggregated career totals (e.g. a projected match outcome, or cumulative goal counts) that must not be mistaken for confirmed results or exact transcription. Spatial constraint: an emphasis-color span (e.g. 'WIN') must stay inline within one text_block and must never be split into its own caption_plate -- colored emphasis is never promoted to an independent claim element.

Do not let the caption_plate plus text_block pairing inside overlay_zone imply the underlying image_region was captured at the moment the quoted line was said -- backstage, podcast, or gym photography is a stock identity image_region, not documentary evidence of when or where the quote occurred. Spatial constraint: the badge (avatar/handle) must stay visually bound to its own caption_plate, and the image_region's anchor_mode must remain static -- it must never take on a cross_slide_locked or timestamp-implying treatment that would suggest synchronized capture.

Do not let a pictured person's gesture inside a comparison_pair (e.g. a reject-hand image_region vs. a pointing-hand image_region) be read as that real person's actual, current, personal endorsement or rejection of the labeled options -- the gesture is a generic template pose repurposed for a binary meme choice, not a captured real opinion. Spatial constraint: each image_region in the comparison_pair must occupy its own hero_zone half with overlap_allowed set to false, and the two halves' text_block labels must never merge into one shared claim.

Do not let an opinion-framed text_block heading (e.g. a 'Hot Take:' label) be dropped or normalized to the same visual certainty as an attributed-quote caption_plate card -- opinion content and attributed-quote content are distinct claim types in this harness and must not collapse into one undifferentiated 'said by X' reading. Spatial constraint: the opinion-label text_block must render at a distinct font_weight and z_index_range above the body text_block, and must never be placed inside the same caption_plate container type used for badge-plus-text_block attribution cards.
